events.text: Your school is the only one in this valley with a roof that does not leak, which is why half the pupils came. You have not yet told them the other half of the roof is next.

choices.text: Teach them to mend roofs first

effects.log: Every pupil learns to mend a roof. It turns out to be a good form for the shoulders.
The roofer stays for three years and learns the spear.

events.text: A farmer pays for his son's lessons at your school in eggs, the eggs in turnips, and the turnips in a goat. The son is very good.

effects.log: The goat becomes the school mascot and the school menace.
The farmer brings eggs anyway, forever.

events.text: Two pupils of your school are in love and have stopped hitting each other properly in practice.

effects.log: They are furious, and improve enormously.
It is the first wedding of the school. You give a terrible speech.

events.text: The magistrate of the county asks your school to keep the peace at the autumn fair. The fair is famous for not being peaceful.

ok.log: There is one brawl and you end it with a look. The magistrate sends wine.

fail.log: There are eleven brawls. You end ten.

effects.log: They manage. They are very proud. The fair is slightly calmer.

events.text: A pupil of your school has run away to join the bandits in the hills because, he says in his note, they have better songs.

effects.log: You find him. The songs really are better. You bring him home and the songs too.
He comes back in a month, thinner, and practices harder than anyone.

events.text: The temple next door to your school complains about the shouting at dawn. The priests are trying to pray to the Maker. You find yourself apologising to the Maker personally, which is a very odd feeling.

choices.text: Move dawn practice to the field

effects.log: The pupils practice in the dew. The priests send cakes.

choices.text: Teach the pupils to shout more quietly

effects.log: There is no such thing, it turns out. They try.

events.text: Your oldest pupil asks to open a branch of your school in the next kingdom. It is a long way, and they are very young, and very ready.

effects.log: The branch opens in spring. Letters come every month, badly spelled and very happy.

choices.text: Ask them to wait a year

effects.log: They wait. They go the next year, better.

events.text: A rich merchant offers to fund your school if it will teach his son, who is lazy, rude and unexpectedly gifted.

choices.text: Take the son, not the money

effects.log: The son is furious to be treated like everyone else. He becomes the best of them.
The school has a new hall. The son remains rude.

events.text: Floodwater in the practice yard of your school. The pupils want to practise anyway, in it.

effects.log: Footwork improves remarkably. So does the laundry.
They bail. They also practise, with buckets.

events.text: You realise one morning that you are the oldest person in your school, and that the pupils have started to speak of the founding as if it were history.

choices.text: Tell them how it really was

effects.log: They do not believe half of it.
The legend is much better than the truth. You keep the truth.

events.text: A travelling master challenges your school at its gate, as travelling masters do. Your pupils look at you.

ok.log: It is a good fight. The master stays a week and teaches a form nobody here knew.

fail.log: The master wins and is very gracious. Your pupils train twice as hard.

effects.log: Your pupil loses, and learns more than in a year.

events.text: Your school has a name now that the villagers use instead of the one you gave it: "the place with the bell". You never had a bell. Somebody has given you one.

effects.log: The temple sends a complaint. The village sets its days by it.

choices.text: Hang it and never ring it

effects.log: It becomes a superstition: the day it rings, something will happen.

events.text: The old master of the school that bowed to yours comes to your gate with his best pupil and a sack of rice, as the custom is. He does not look at you. He looks at your yard, measuring it.

effects.log: He is startled. At the next festival he stands beside you without being asked.
All is correct. He goes away still measuring.

events.text: The pupils of the school under yours and the pupils of your own have been fighting in the market. Nobody started it, everybody says.

effects.log: There are three weeks of bruises and then a friendship.
Both sides are united against you. It is a start.

events.text: The school under yours keeps its own name on its gate. Some of your pupils want it painted over.

effects.log: It stays. The old master thanks you once, years later, in a single word.
A compromise. Nobody likes it. It lasts.

events.text: The best pupil the school under yours sends you this spring is better than any of your own.

effects.log: They become your heir in all but name.
They go home. The school under yours becomes famous, and stays loyal.

events.text: A third school in the county asks whether it, too, might come under yours, without being made to. It is a strange thing to be asked.

effects.log: Your schools are three now. The county starts to call it a family.
They are relieved. You share a festival instead.

events.text: The old master of the school under yours dies. His pupils ask you to speak at the grave.

choices.text: Speak of what he did well

effects.log: You speak for a long time. His pupils are yours, in the end, because of it.
They speak. You only bow. It is enough.

events.text: A lord of the kingdom notices that your school now has many halls and asks what you intend by it.

ok.log: He is satisfied, and asks you to teach his guard.

fail.log: He is not satisfied. He watches you for years.

effects.log: He comes. He is terrible. He is delighted.

events.text: The school under yours wants to break away again. The old resentment has come back with a new generation.

effects.log: They go. A year later they come back, because they wanted to choose.
They stay. They are quiet. You wonder for how long.

events.text: The old master of {b3_school} sits in the best chair of the house, drinks the tea in one swallow, and looks at your hands for a long time. "These," the master says, to nobody in particular. "These will do."

choices.text: Bow and say you will come

effects.log: The master nods once and leaves without finishing the cakes. The cook is furious about the cakes. You pack that night.

choices.text: Ask what the hands will do

effects.log: "Everything you let them," says the master. You think about that answer for years.

events.text: A pupil of {b3_school} has been watching you carry water for a week. On the eighth day the pupil comes to the well with a letter from the master, very crumpled from being held so long.

effects.log: It is four lines long and says you are wanted. You read it until the ink runs.

choices.text: Ask the pupil what the school is like

effects.log: The pupil talks for an hour, mostly about the food. It sounds wonderful.

events.text: The house argues all evening about the offer from {b3_school}. An old grandmother settles it by asking you, which nobody else had thought of doing.

effects.log: The old woman nods as if she had known. She gives you her own mother's hairpin for the road.
The master of {b3_school} sends word that a year is fine. You are not sure you deserved that.

events.text: Two schools want you: {b3_school}, whose master came in person, and a richer one whose master sent a cart. The village has opinions.

choices.text: Go with the one who came

effects.log: The rich school is offended for a month. You never regret it.

choices.text: Ask both masters to test you

ok.log: They test you together and end up drinking together. Both schools become your friends.

fail.log: They both find you a little forward. You keep the first offer anyway.

events.text: On the first morning at {b3_school} you are told you were not tested like the others, and three pupils have decided to test you themselves, behind the woodshed.

ok.log: You lose, but not by much, and stand up every time. By evening they are your friends.

fail.log: You lose badly. You go back the next day. They respect that more than winning.

effects.log: The master hears you out, then sends you behind the woodshed anyway. "Go on," the master says. "It is part of it."

events.text: In the night {npc} breaks through to {npc_realm}, and by morning the whole valley knows: the miller heard a shout, the miller's wife saw a light. The pupils of your school have already borrowed every lantern in the village.

choices.text: Throw a feast for the whole valley

effects.log: The valley comes. {npc} is toasted until {he} hides in the hayloft. It is a very good night.

choices.text: Give {him} your own old practice sword

effects.log: It is notched and too short and {he} will never use another. {npc} cannot say anything at all.

events.text: {npc} comes to breakfast at {npc_realm} as if nothing has happened, and drops the bowl, because the hands are not used to being that strong yet. Everyone at the long table pretends not to notice, very loudly.

effects.log: No lessons, a roast, and a race to the river that {npc} loses on purpose. Nobody believes {him}.

choices.text: Make {him} wash every bowl in the school

effects.log: {He} does, laughing, and breaks only three. The juniors call it the Feast of Bowls for years.

events.text: Word of {npc}'s breakthrough to {npc_realm} reaches the temple of the Maker before it reaches you, and the priest arrives with a blessing, a cake and a list of the temple's leaks.

choices.text: Feast in the temple yard, and mend the roof after

effects.log: A feast and a roof in one week. The priest blesses {npc} twice, to be sure.

choices.text: Keep it in the school, quietly

effects.log: A small supper, the senior pupils only, and one speech you will remember longer than {npc} will.

events.text: {npc} asks to walk with you along the river. At the bend {he} stops. "The villages past the hills have no school. I want to build one there, in your name, with your forms. A branch, not a new tree."

choices.text: Give your blessing and your seal

effects.log: You cut the seal yourself, badly. A year later there are thirty children in a barn past the hills, all standing the way you stand.

choices.text: Give {him} your own notebook of forms

effects.log: It is the one with the coffee rings and the swearing in the margins. {npc} carries it like an egg. The branch is famous in ten years.

events.text: A letter in {npc}'s careful hand: the market town by the ford has asked for a teacher, the magistrate has found a hall, and would you allow it to be a branch of your school.

choices.text: Allow it, and go to the opening

effects.log: You walk two days to stand at the back. {npc} sees you and forgets the whole speech. It is a good school.

choices.text: Allow it, with one condition: {he} comes home every new year

effects.log: {He} comes home every new year for the rest of your life, with a cart of pupils who want to see the old master.

events.text: In the practice yard, an ordinary morning, {npc} turns your strike aside and you are simply not quick enough any more. {npc}, {npc_realm} now, stands very still, waiting to be scolded.

choices.text: Laugh, get up and bow to your student

effects.log: "That," you say, "is the whole point of me." {npc} cries. The juniors have never seen either of you so happy.

choices.text: Ask {him} to show you what {he} did

effects.log: The student teaches the master, badly, too kindly. You learn it anyway. The whole school watches.

events.text: {npc} has been winning the bouts at the spring fair that you used to win, and coming home quieter each time, as if apologising. Tonight {he} cannot finish supper.

choices.text: Tell {him} you have been waiting for this for years

effects.log: {He} looks up. You see {him} put something heavy down. The next fair {he} wins grinning.

choices.text: Challenge {him} in front of the school, and lose properly

effects.log: You lose properly, which is harder than it looks. The school cheers you both.
